description: Trend Detective tests 46 years of NASA MERRA-2 data to find which climate trends are real and which are just luck. Using the overfitting checks quant traders rely on, we put 12,960 places and nine variables through a trend test, a shuffled-noise luck test, false-discovery control, El Niño removal, and an out-of-sample backtest. Results come alive on an interactive 3D globe where fake trends dissolve, so anyone can see which changes on Earth are real signal and which are noise.
summary: 46 years of NASA MERRA-2 data show trends almost everywhere, but many are just luck. Trend Detective puts every place on Earth through the same overfitting checks quant traders use before trusting a strategy: an autocorrelation-aware trend test, a shuffled-noise luck test, false-discovery control, El Niño removal, and an out-of-sample backtest. What survives is shown on an interactive 3D globe that separates real climate signal from noise.
details:
Give any noisy dataset to someone looking for a trend and they will find one. That is the problem this challenge asks us to solve. Trend Detective treats every point on Earth like an unproven trading strategy: 12,960 grid squares, nine MERRA-2 variables (air temperature, water vapor, rain and snow, evaporation, soil moisture, snow on the ground, surface runoff, haze and dust), 1980–2025.

Every place goes through five checks:

1. Simple test: Mann-Kendall with the Hamed–Rao autocorrelation correction, plus a Theil–Sen slope with a confidence interval.

2. Luck test: we shuffle each place's years to destroy any real trend and test again. For air temperature, 640 "trends" still appear in pure noise, which shows how many false alarms you'd get by chance.

3. Strict test: Benjamini–Hochberg false-discovery control across the whole map. 9,588 apparent temperature trends become 8,834 real ones.

4. El Niño removal: we regress out NOAA's Niño 3.4 index, the way a trader removes market beta, to check that a trend isn't just Pacific weather swings.

5. Out-of-sample backtest: find trends in 1980–2002, then check them on 2003–2025, data they never saw. 70% of temperature trends held up (1,610 of 2,296).

What you can do on the site:

- Interactive 3D globe: columns rise and fall with each trend, false alarms flash violet, and fake trends dissolve during the strict test. Switch between all nine variables, colour by out-of-sample result, or play the years 1980–2025.

- "Which variables can you trust?": a leaderboard of the share of trends that are real. Water vapor (94%) and temperature (92%) are almost all real; snow on the ground (35%) is mostly not.

- Guided tour: a 30-second automatic walkthrough of the whole investigation.

- Case studies such as the Arctic: +0.44 °C/decade, about 2.7× the global rate in MERRA-2 (observations give about 3.8×; Rantanen et al. 2022), surviving both El Niño removal and the backtest.

- Check your hometown: search 1,251 cities and get the verdict for every variable (real signal, could be luck, or no trend).

- The Lab, Fool the Detector: hide a trend in random noise and see which tests catch it.

- Open data: download any case as a CSV, and share any view as a link with its own preview image.
